problem.question: Don buys recyclable bottles in a small town. Shop A normally sells him 150 bottles, shop B sells him 180 bottles and Shop C sells him the rest. How many bottles does Don buy from Shop C if he is capable of buying only 550 bottles?
problem.answer:
Between Shop A and Shop B he buys 150 bottles+180 bottles=<<150+180=330>>330 bottles
Thus he can buy 550 bottles-330 bottles=<<550-330=220>>220 bottles from shop C
#### 220

generation.text:
Don buys 150 bottles from shop A and 180 bottles from shop B, a total of 150+180 = 330 bottles
He is capable of buying only 550 bottles, so he has 550-330 = 220 bottles left to buy from Shop C
The final answer is \boxed{220}.
